newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares edge to higher close in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares edge to higher close in thin trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange edged up Monday in thin trade as players remained sidelined due to caution ahead of first quarter company financial results and jitters over a possible U.S. interest rate hike, brokers said.
They added the market would likely see low volumes and broadly stable prices this week.

The blue-chip index rose 0.16 percent to 2.548,46 points, while the general index climbed 0.04 percent to 1,745.53 points, according to preliminary figures. Volume was a low 23.0 million soles ($8.6 million).
"Everyone is sitting tight on their positions. Many investors are on the sidelines until the financial results are known," said Miguel Bondy of local brokerage JPBT.
"The volume's not too bad," said broker Pablo Navarro brokerage Fortuna.
Brewery Cerveza Nacional de Cerveza jumped 2.22 percent to 1.38 soles, with 993,866 shares traded, while Backus y Johnston gained 1.79 percent to 2.27 soles with 231,839 shares traded.
Holding company Credicorp closed up 2.11 percent to $20.83 with 50,663 shares exchanged.
Polymetal mining firm Morococha rose 2.53 percent to 2.70 soles, with 157,913 shares traded, while Atacocha gained 1.57 percent to 1.25 soles, with 137.575 shares changing hands.
Electricity firm Edegel was up 1.53 percent at 1.29 soles, with 287.774 shares traded.
